feedback.problem: Consider a linear transformation $\,T\,.$ If $\,{v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0\,$ and $\,T({v}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\,$, find $\,T(7{v}_{1}-5{v}_{2}).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, since ${v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0,$ we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}7{v}_{1}-5{v}_{2} & =12{v}_{1}-5{v}_{1}-5{v}_{2} \\  & =12{v}_{1}-5({v}_{1}+{v}_{2}) \\  & =12{v}_{1}-5(0) \\  & =12{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
T(7{v}_{1}-5{v}_{2})=T(12{v}_{1}).
$$

Now, since $T$ is a linear transformation, we have that $T(kv)=kT(v).$ So 

$$
\begin{aligned}T(12{v}_{1}) & =12T({v}_{1}) \\  & =12[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 24 \\ -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, $T(7{v}_{1}-5{v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 24 \\ -12\end{aligned}].$
